market_label: products with metal parts: automotive, hardware, electrical, appliances

prompts.opening_context: It is reaching out to a company that builds products with small metal parts in them and might buy special cold-formed parts for them.
prompts.relevance_intro: {name} makes special cold-formed fasteners and precision metal parts to its customers' drawings. Its clients are companies in EUROPE that design and build products with small metal parts in them (car door and window systems, furniture and window hardware, electrical and electronic components, appliances and similar) and could buy those parts from {name}.
relevance_no: it is itself a MAKER or DISTRIBUTOR of screws, bolts, rivets, pins or other fasteners or cold-formed parts: it sells what {name} sells, so it is a competitor, not a buyer;

it is a news or media site, a job board, a directory, a school, a car dealer or garage, a shop selling to consumers, or a company that does not design or build physical products with metal parts in them.
relevance_yes: a manufacturer, OEM, or Tier-1 or Tier-2 supplier that builds products or assemblies with metal parts in them, in automotive, furniture or window hardware, electrical or electronics, appliances, bicycles, energy, machinery or a similar industry;
an engineering or assembly company that buys metal components made to its drawings;
a company of these kinds whose text does not say where it is based.
prompts.relevance_judge_note: Judge by what the company does, not by a word in its name: a company that makes locks, hinges or connectors uses fasteners but does not sell them, so it is a buyer.
prompts.country_context: an Italian maker of cold-formed metal parts
prompts.strategist_targets: (manufacturers, OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers that build products with small metal parts: car door and window systems, furniture and window hardware, electrical components, appliances, e-bikes, solar mounting, heat pumps) that might buy special cold-formed parts from {name}
prompts.strategist_verticals: car door and window systems, furniture and window hardware, electrical and electronic components, household appliances, motorcycles and bicycles, solar mounting, heat pumps, machinery
prompts.strategist_query_rule: Each query = a product the company BUILDS + "manufacturer" (or OEM / Tier 1 supplier) + a European country. Do NOT search for fasteners, screws, bolts, cold forming, viteria, Schrauben or Verbindungselemente, nor for distributors or wholesalers: a search for what {name} sells finds its competitors.

sectors.name: Automotive Tier-1s: door, window and cockpit systems
sectors.why_omega_fits: Omega's largest sector: for over 40 years it has supplied safety parts for car door and window systems (door locking systems, door modules, window regulators, instrument panels). It is IATF 16949 certified and holds stock in Germany and the Czech Republic.
barriers: IATF 16949 already held, so no certification gap
Shrinking EU vehicle volumes and Tier-1 cost pressure
New parts are won only at new model launches (sourcing cycles of several years)

demand_evidence.claim: Germany, Omega's largest market, built 4.151M cars in 2025 (+2%), 40% of them electric.
CLEPA survey: 24% of European automotive suppliers expect losses in 2026, and 40% have raised their non-automotive exposure.
EU car production is about 2.6M units (-19%) below its 2019 level.

sectors.name: Furniture fittings and furniture makers
sectors.why_omega_fits: Working with its customers, Omega has developed parts for the opening and closing mechanisms of furniture, used by leading European manufacturers. Cold forming suits the large series these products need.
barriers: No sector certification required; ISO 9001 normally sufficient (UNVERIFIED per buyer)
Flat demand tied to housing and kitchen markets
Strong price pressure from Asian component imports
buyer_roles: Product Development Engineer, hinges and runners

demand_evidence.claim: Blum (AT) turnover rose 2.4% to EUR 2,495M in the financial year ended 30 June 2026.
Hettich (DE) turnover was EUR 1.4bn in 2025, down about 2% nominal (flat at constant currency); it expects no quick, broad market recovery in 2026.

sectors.name: Window and door hardware makers
sectors.why_omega_fits: Omega has developed parts for the opening and closing mechanisms of windows together with its customers, used by leading European manufacturers.
barriers: No sector certification required (UNVERIFIED per buyer)
Demand tied to new-build and renovation, both weak since 2023
Buyers are concentrated: a handful of hardware groups
buyer_roles: Commodity Buyer, turned and formed parts

en: lift and slide door system manufacturer

demand_evidence.claim: VFF forecasts the German window market to grow 1.9-3.1% in 2026, to 13.28M window units in the base scenario, an upgrade on its October 2025 study.
Roto Group reported a slight decline in 2025 net turnover, while turnover rose slightly in almost all EU countries.

sectors.name: Electrical and electronic equipment (switchgear, connectors, installation devices)
sectors.why_omega_fits: Omega makes precision components for electrical and electronic assemblies, made and checked in the same plant as its automotive parts, from wire 0.5 to 25 mm including brass.
barriers: IEC/UL product approvals sit with the OEM, but parts may need material and plating declarations (RoHS/REACH)
Large OEMs run formal supplier approval and audits

demand_evidence.claim: ENTSO-E's 2026 supply-chain report: TSOs plan 4,238 SF6-free GIS bays, 10,819 AIS circuit breakers and 2,820 new power transformers to 2035, and ask manufacturers to scale capacity.
ABB is investing about USD 200M over three years in European medium-voltage manufacturing, including about USD 100M for a new switchgear plant in Dalmine, Italy.

sectors.name: Motorcycle and scooter makers and their suppliers
sectors.why_omega_fits: Omega's parts are already used in motorcycles, and it makes stepped pins and axles, bushings and sleeves, and special threaded studs to customer drawings.
barriers: Falling registrations in 2025
Smaller series than cars; some OEMs ask for IATF-style PPAP (IATF already held)

demand_evidence.claim: Motorcycle registrations in the five key European markets fell 12.9% to 1,002,848 in 2025 (Germany -35.7%, Italy -6%), though still above 2019.

sectors.name: Household appliance makers
sectors.why_omega_fits: Omega's parts are already used in household appliances, and cold forming gives large series with little waste and a low cost per part.
barriers: Weak, price-driven market with rising Asian imports
No sector certification required (UNVERIFIED per buyer)

demand_evidence.claim: APPLiA: European home appliance sales ended 2025 at roughly 170M units, back to 2015 levels; four member states asked the Commission for a sector action plan.
Italy's appliance replacement bonus added 194,600 unit sales (+8.8%) from Nov 2025 to Apr 2026; over 52% of eligible EU products were made in Italy.

sectors.name: Eyewear makers
sectors.why_omega_fits: Omega's parts are already used in eyewear; it forms wire from 0.5 mm with tolerances as tight as a hundredth of a millimetre.
barriers: Small parts, small volumes per model; many makers source micro parts locally in the Belluno district
Cosmetic surface and plating requirements

demand_evidence.claim: ANFAO pre-estimate: Italian eyewear production was EUR 5.64bn in 2025, stable; exports fell 3.9% but Europe took over 59% of exports and grew 8.1%.
Italian eyewear exports fell 6.1% to EUR 1.34bn in Q1 2026.

sectors.name: Heat pump and HVAC equipment makers
sectors.why_omega_fits: Omega already supplies household appliance and electrical parts, works in carbon and stainless steel, aluminium and brass, and sorts finished parts 100%.
barriers: No sector-specific certification found; ISO 9001 likely sufficient (UNVERIFIED)
Demand swings with national subsidies (2025 declines in France and Poland)
Outdoor units need corrosion-resistant parts and finishes

demand_evidence.claim: EHPA: heat pump sales in 21 European countries rose 13% to 2.88M in 2025; Germany grew 50% and heat pumps reached half its space-heating market.

sectors.name: Rail rolling stock and rail subsystem makers
sectors.why_omega_fits: Omega's parts go into products where a single defective piece can stop an assembly line; every press monitors its forming force and finished parts are sorted 100%.
barriers: ISO/TS 22163 (IRIS) increasingly expected of rail suppliers
First-article inspection and long qualification cycles
Smaller series than automotive, which weakens the cold-forming cost advantage

demand_evidence.claim: UNIFE World Rail Market Study 2024: global rail supply growth in 2021-2023 was largely driven by Western Europe, up 7.3% a year.
Europe is now the world's largest regional railway market at EUR 77.7bn, growing above average on network renewal (SCI Verkehr data).
demand_evidence.date: 2026-09 (approx., published around InnoTrans; exact day UNVERIFIED)

sectors.name: EV charging hardware and charging connector makers
sectors.why_omega_fits: Omega makes precision components for electrical assemblies in brass and other metals, and plans to offer turned parts in their own right alongside cold-formed ones.
barriers: Connector contacts are often turned and silver-plated; Omega's turned-parts offer is still a plan
RoHS/REACH declarations for brass and platings
Fragmented, consolidating maker base; growth may slow after AFIR targets are met

it: produttore infrastrutture di ricarica per veicoli elettrici

demand_evidence.claim: The EU had about 1.1M public charging points at the end of 2025, roughly five times the 2020 number.
T&E: charging infrastructure has far outpaced EV sales in all but one EU country, a sign that charger build-out may slow.

sectors.name: Defence and aerospace systems makers
sectors.why_omega_fits: Omega states it is opening its cold-forming know-how to aerospace and defence supply chains and welcomes supply-chain enquiries, but does not yet hold certifications specific to these sectors.
barriers: EN 9100 (AS9100) required for aerospace; Omega does not hold it
NATO AQAP 2110 often requested in defence contracts (UNVERIFIED per buyer)
Export control, security vetting and long qualification
Diversification already stalled once

demand_evidence.claim: The EU SAFE instrument provides up to EUR 150bn in defence loans; at least 65% of component costs must originate in the EU, Ukraine or eligible EEA/EFTA countries.
Horváth Defense Study 2026: 89% of defence executives call supply-chain resilience a central priority and 94% see supplier capacity-expansion speed as decisive.
